about: Which e2e spec files a pull request runs for a changed path of src/ or harness/ (scripts/ci-scope.mjs, e2eSpecs). A changed path that no rule matches runs every spec file, and so does any other app path (a helper of test/e2e, a fixture, the Playwright config, a build input, package.json). A rule is added only when the code under its globs is seen by e2e tests through its spec files alone; when in doubt, leave the path out. test/contract/ci-scope-e2e.test.ts checks that every glob matches a file and every spec file exists.

rules.why: The app reads its Harness copy (out/harness, src/main/harness/bundled.ts) only to install or migrate it (ipc/harness.ts, ipc/harness-migration.ts), for profiles/draft.schema.json (ipc/projects.ts) and for its version; e2e sessions run the fake agent. These specs copy out/harness or install it and run its scripts (finder-path: bin/profile, bin/ticket, bin/epic-status; projects-connect: bin/project-connect, bin/profile; first-run: profile --help), read hooks/rules and .mcp.json (harness-migrate, select through legacy-claude-home.ts) check the Harness status (settings-health, toolbar), or check the executable bits of out/harness (packaged.spec.ts, its untagged block for the dev run of the unpacked build, expectHarnessCopy). Every other spec writes its own stub scripts. Left out on purpose: .claude-plugin/ (the version every spec sees) and package.json.

The link between machines: its remote paths run only with a linked machine, in the specs that pair two apps (linkThroughUi, launchLinkedPair) or open the Linked machines settings: the linked-* specs, family.spec.ts, controls.spec.ts and browser-family.spec.ts; sidebar-sections and focus-sidebar show the Link machine button, autopilot.spec.ts reaches service.ts through ipc/autopilot.ts. Left out: caller.ts and messages.ts (every ipc handler calls through them), ipc-adapter.ts (browser/read-only.ts, read by ipc/layout.ts for every canvas) and autopilot-runs.ts (ipc/autopilot.ts).

The Browser node and its layer: web pages in the app, seen by the browser* specs, linked-browser.spec.ts and controls.spec.ts (a Browser node among the controls). Left out: read-only.ts (ipc/layout.ts), cdp.ts and origins.ts (the MCP server of every agent session), shared/browser/* and renderer browser-frame.ts and profiles.ts (the menu that creates nodes, create-items.ts).

The preset of a plan (worfy-throughput ticket 42): only Settings → Plan reads it (planPreset.read) and writes it (planPreset.apply), and settings.spec.ts is the spec that opens that section. Every other spec loads src/main/ipc/plan-preset.ts with the IPC handlers, which only subscribes the plan to the Sessions and to will-quit; a module that failed to load would fail settings.spec.ts too, which launches the app.
